record.context_brief: characterizing admissible orderings of Gabor frames
record.original_question: Given an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, which orderings {f_k}_{k in I} of its elements have the property that the ordered frame can be represented as an operator orbit {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for some bounded linear operator T? In other words, can one characterize exactly which permutations or sequential arrangements of the same Gabor frame yield a bounded generating operator?

evidence.quote: (P1-b) Can we characterize the orderings {fk}k∈I of {EmbTnag}m,n∈Z for which a representation as in (2.3) is available with a bounded operator T?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and let $a, b > 0$. For $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, define the modulation and translation operators on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ by
$$(E_{mb} h)(x) = e^{2\pi i m b x} h(x), \qquad (T_{na} h)(x) = h(x - na),$$
and consider the Gabor system $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b) = \{E_{mb} T_{na} g\}_{m,n \in \mathbb{Z}}$. Assume that $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, that is, it is a frame but not a Riesz basis.

Given a countable index set $I$ (either $\mathbb{N}$ or $\mathbb{Z}$) and a bijection $\sigma : I \to \mathbb{Z}^2$, set $f_k := E_{\sigma(k)_1 b} T_{\sigma(k)_2 a} g$ for $k \in I$, so that $\{f_k\}_{k \in I}$ is an enumeration (ordering) of $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$.

Characterize precisely those orderings $\{f_k\}_{k \in I}$ of $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ for which there exists a bounded linear operator $T : L^2(\mathbb{R}) \to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and an element $\varphi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that
$$f_k = T^k \varphi \quad \text{for all } k \in I,$$
i.e., the ordered frame coincides with the orbit $\{T^k \varphi\}_{k \in I}$ of $\varphi$ under iteration of $T$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has seen significant partial progress but no full characterization. It is known that an overcomplete Gabor frame indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ cannot be represented as $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ with a bounded operator $T$. For the two-sided case ($I=\mathbb{Z}$), a general criterion states that an ordered frame $\{f_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is an orbit of a bounded bijective operator iff $\langle f_i, h_j\rangle = \langle f_{i+1}, h_{j+1}\rangle$ for all $i,j$, where $\{h_k\}$ is the canonical dual. Using this, follow-up work (Christensen–Hasannasab–Stoeva, Cabrelli–Molter–Romero, et al., 2018–2020) showed several negative results, e.g. when $ab \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ no ordering of $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ comes from a bounded invertible operator. A complete characterization of admissible orderings remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Orbits of bounded bijective operators and Gabor frames
status_evidence.snippet: If G(g,a,b) is a Gabor frame such that ab ∈ ℝ\ℚ, then G(g,a,b), with any ordering over ℤ, is not generated by an operator in GL(L2(ℝ)).
status_evidence.claim: Negative result for irrational ab: no ordering yields a bounded invertible generator.

status_evidence.title: Frame Properties of Operator Orbits
status_evidence.snippet: A frame {fn}n∈ℤ is an orbit of an operator in GL(H) iff ⟨fi,hj⟩=⟨fi+1,hj+1⟩ for all i,j.
status_evidence.claim: General criterion for bounded invertible operator orbit representations.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical sampling and frame representations with bounded operators
status_evidence.snippet: An overcomplete Gabor or wavelet frame can never be written as (T^n f0)_{n∈ℕ} with bounded T; the case I=ℤ remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Half-line case is fully resolved (negatively); two-sided case open.
